nodes.description: Chronic joint pain is common and, with mobility limitation, is what most affects daily life; it is managed jointly by orthopaedics and physiatry.

evidence.snippet: Limited joint mobility and chronic pain are common.

nodes.description: Developmental coxa vara, and the direct cause of the waddling gait. Rare in classical Sutcliffe-type disease but characteristic of the FN1-related form.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in Fibronectin Cause a Subtype of Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia with "Corner Fractures".
evidence.snippet: The severe scoliosis in most individuals and rare developmental coxa vara distinguish individuals with FN1 mutations from those with classical Sutcliffe-type SMD.

nodes.description: The reported SMDCF variants cluster in the N-terminal 70 kDa assembly region of fibronectin and share a mechanism: they substitute cysteine residues in the type-I assembly domains, disrupting the disulfide bonds that domain folding depends on. Five novel variants reported in one series were all cysteine substitutions in that region, which is a strong constraint for a gene as large as FN1.
nodes.id: Cysteine-Substituting FN1 Variants in the N-Terminal Assembly Region

evidence.reference_title: Novel fibronectin mutations and expansion of the phenotype in spondylometaphyseal dysplasia with "corner fractures".
evidence.snippet: All individuals shared a substitution of a cysteine residue, disrupting disulfide bonds in the FN type-I assembly domains located in the N-terminal assembly region.

nodes.description: Fibronectin is the master organiser of extracellular matrix, nucleating the assembly of collagens and fibrillin-1, and it is secreted in the skeleton by osteoblasts, chondrocytes and mesenchymal cells. Reduced fibronectin matrix therefore degrades the scaffold on which cartilage and bone matrix is built, which is why a ubiquitously expressed matrix protein produces a skeleton-restricted disease.
nodes.id: Deficient Fibronectin Matrix Assembly in Cartilage and Bone

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in Fibronectin Cause a Subtype of Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia with "Corner Fractures".
evidence.snippet: Fibronectin is a master organizer of extracellular matrices (ECMs) and promotes the assembly of collagens, fibrillin-1, and other proteins. It is also known to play roles in skeletal tissues through its secretion by osteoblasts, chondrocytes, and mesenchymal cells.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in Fibronectin Cause a Subtype of Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia with "Corner Fractures".
evidence.snippet: In summary, FN1 mutations that cause defective fibronectin secretion are found in SMD, and we thus provide additional evidence for a critical function of fibronectin in cartilage and bone.

evidence.reference_title: Novel fibronectin mutations and expansion of the phenotype in spondylometaphyseal dysplasia with "corner fractures".
evidence.snippet: Here we report five patients affected by this subtype of SMD-CF caused by five novel FN1 missense mutations: p.Cys123Tyr, p.Cys169Tyr, p.Cys213Tyr, p.Cys231Trp and p.Cys258Tyr.

nodes.description: Vision impairment and glaucoma have been reported, and annual intraocular pressure measurement is recommended specifically in FN1-related disease. This is the extra-skeletal feature most likely to be missed.

evidence.snippet: Vision impairment and glaucoma have been reported.

nodes.description: Mutant fibronectin is held in the secretory pathway - specifically in the endoplasmic reticulum in patient dermal fibroblasts - so much less reaches the extracellular space. The effect is quantitative rather than absolute: mutant protein is detectable in patient plasma and culture medium, just at much lower abundance than wild type.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanistic insights into the cellular effects of a novel FN1 variant associated with a spondylometaphyseal dysplasia.
evidence.snippet: Using mass spectroscopy, mutant FN was detected in plasma and in culture medium of primary dermal fibroblasts isolated from the patient, but mutant protein was much less abundant than wild-type FN.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanistic insights into the cellular effects of a novel FN1 variant associated with a spondylometaphyseal dysplasia.
evidence.snippet: mutant FN was preferentially retained within the endoplasmic reticulum

nodes.description: Enlarged metaphyses with triangular ossification defects at their margins, giving the appearance of healing corner fractures. The name is a radiographic description, not a mechanism: these are modelling defects, and in one reported patient the distal femoral changes healed with skeletal maturation.
nodes.id: Metaphyseal Ossification Defect Resembling Corner Fractures

evidence.snippet: Radiographic features include enlargement and corner fracture-like lesions of the metaphyses, developmental coxa vara, shortened long bones, scoliosis, and vertebral anomalies.

evidence.reference_title: Novel fibronectin mutations and expansion of the phenotype in spondylometaphyseal dysplasia with "corner fractures".
evidence.snippet: Interestingly, the distal femoral changes in this patient healed with skeletal maturation.

nodes.description: Annual intraocular pressure and blood pressure measurement, recommended specifically for FN1-related disease. This is the part of management a skeletal-dysplasia clinic would not otherwise do.

evidence.snippet: Annual evaluation of intraocular pressure and blood pressure in individuals with FN1-related SMDCF.

nodes.description: Surgical treatment for coxa vara, genu valgum or varum, tibial bowing, leg length discrepancy and atlantoaxial instability, plus standard scoliosis management. This is the main intervention in the disease.

evidence.snippet: Annual evaluation by an orthopedist and/or physiatrist for scoliosis, other orthopedic complications, mobility issues, and chronic pain.

nodes.description: Chronic joint pain and mobility limitation are managed jointly by orthopaedics, physiatry and physical therapy, with avoidance of activities that strain painful joints.

evidence.snippet: management of mobility issues and chronic joint pain by orthopedist and/or physiatrist and physical therapist

nodes.description: Short stature, present at birth or developing in early infancy, with a waddling gait, developmental coxa vara, severe scoliosis, limited joint mobility and chronic pain. Severe scoliosis and developmental coxa vara are what distinguish FN1-related disease from the classical Sutcliffe-type description.
nodes.id: Short Stature with Coxa Vara, Scoliosis and Joint Disease

evidence.snippet: Short stature may be present at birth or develop in early infancy. Individuals may present with short limbs and/or short trunk. Radiographic features include enlargement and corner fracture-like lesions of the metaphyses, developmental coxa vara, shortened long bones, scoliosis, and vertebral anomalies. Limited joint mobility and chronic pain are common.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in Fibronectin Cause a Subtype of Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia with "Corner Fractures".
evidence.snippet: The severe scoliosis in most individuals and rare developmental coxa vara distinguish individuals with FN1 mutations from those with classical Sutcliffe-type SMD.
